text:
incident-bot: ALERT: hotpath GPU pool 'hotpath-1' reporting sustained queue growth and client 429s. Thresholds breached: queue > 8k, 429 spike => 18% over 5m. Paging sre_oncall.

sre_oncall: on it. grabbing dashboards now. starting timeline in thread.

maya (eng-runtime): I'm seeing GPU util ~100% on hotpath-1, few nodes OOM-killed earlier. queue length 12.1k, p50 latency steady, tail skyrocketing. spikes at 14:04 UTC.

sam (autoscale): autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but all hit MaxNodesReached and a lock wait. cooldown timers also stacking. looks like a deadlock where scale-out inhibited while tokenbucket is starving requests.

li (eng-infra): quick check of rate limiter config: recent deploy (08:12) set token_refill_ms from 1000 -> 10000 for prod hotpath tier. commit 3f2b9e altered default. That slows refill 10x.

jordan (customer-success): getting multiple customer reports: "requests failing with 429s" for both hosted API and dedicated customers on that tier. CS triage opened INC-5231.

sre_oncall: confirm root cause hypothesis: tokenbucket refill was reduced, reducing effective throughput; autoscaler attempted to react but hit max_nodes and cooldown prevented further scaling => queue growth => more 429s.

maya (eng-runtime): can we temporarily bypass tokenbucket for 'dedicated-latency' tier? we should also increase max_nodes and lift cooldown for autoscaler while we recover.

sam (autoscale): need infra approval for emergency max_nodes bump. propose: max_nodes += 6, cooldown override to 30s, and remove the lockfile preventing concurrent scale. I'll prepare patch.

li (eng-infra): applying emergency changes. patching config now.

ops-bot: command executed by li: `kubectl -n infra patch cm rate-limiter-config --patch '{"data":{"token_refill_ms":"1000"}}'`

ops-bot: command executed by li: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment/autoscaler --replicas=12`

ops-bot: autoscaler lockfile removed: `/var/run/autoscaler.lock` deleted on 3 nodes.

maya (eng-runtime): temporarily set bypass flag on hotpath tier so tier-level rate checks are disabled for 10m: `redwood-config set tiers.hotpath.bypass_rate_limit true --duration 10m`

jordan (customer-success): posting intermediate customer update: "We're aware of increased errors, mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15m."

sre_oncall: monitoring metrics: queue length trending down from 12.1k -> 4.3k in 6 minutes. 429 rate dropping from 18% -> 4% in same window. good sign.

sam (autoscale): autoscaler is scaling out successfully now, nodes added: +6 new GPU nodes. No further MaxNodesReached errors. Cooldown in logs shows override applied.

li (eng-infra): revert token_refill to 1000 in config permanently and mark the deploy that changed it for rollback review. Created PR #642_fix-token-refill.

maya (eng-runtime): root cause: accidental config change in a production merge that increased token_refill_ms. It effectively lowered throughput and interacted badly with strict tier-based token buckets and autoscaler caps.

jordan (customer-success): customers reporting requests are returning to normal. continuing monitoring.

sre_oncall: we'll keep incident open for postmortem. next steps: rollback the code change, add a canary gating for rate-limiter config, add alert for token_refill_ms drift, and run a chaos test for autoscaler lock contention.

ops-bot: Incident severity set to S2 by sre_oncall.

sam (autoscale): follow-up actions I logged: add metric for `autoscaler.lock_wait_seconds`, add auto-resync that clears stale locks older than 2m, and improve error message when MaxNodesReached occurs.

li (eng-infra): I deployed a telemetry alert: `tokenbucket.refill_ms > 2000` for any hotpath tier will page infra.

maya (eng-runtime): will submit PR to prevent config drift and to add structured deploy review for rate limiting.

jordan (customer-success): sending final customer note: "Issue mitigated, errors returning to expected levels. We'll share a follow-up with root cause and timeline."

ops-bot: summary log: emergency scale +6 nodes, token_refill_ms rollback, tokenbucket bypass applied briefly, autoscaler locks cleared.

sre_oncall: handing off to li for the next 30m for watch. @li please ack and run postmortem doc.

li (eng-infra): ack. I'll draft the incident report and include timeline + config diff + customer impact numbers.

jordan (customer-success): noted. I'll sync CS notes with the postmortem.

ops-bot: Thread closed for immediate action; will reopen if metrics worsen.

sre_oncall: thanks everyone. good coordination. follow-up: postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
